We love supporting our local farmers, and offer seasonal desserts so they are at their peak of freshness. We are passionate about creating fresh, decadent desserts, and seeing our clients smile. Our specialty are cheesecakes and cakes. We have over 50 flavors, and are always creating new flavors. rate that exceeded our capacity at the original Blue Mountain location in Afton. The next evolution for us became Blue Mountain Barrel House, a larger production-minded facility with almost tenfold capacity of our brewery in Afton. But just building a bigger brewery seemed a bit boring. So we did things our way: first, we picked a 15-acre spot in the south of Nelson County that has the stunning mountain views to match our Afton location. As the most mountainous county in America east of the Mississippi, the stark line of the Blue Ridge is woven into the fabric of our inspiration. Next, we designed a facility that had special capabilities to produce the barrel-aged beers we hang our hat on, beers like Dark Hollow. With a unique brewhouse and a fluctuating temperature-controlled barrel aging room, Blue Mountain Barrel House operates one of the largest barrel-aging facilities on the east coast. Visit us seven days a week in the Barrel House tasting room with inside seating, ever-rotating draft beers and a cornucopia of bottled offerings, plus spacious outdoor seating with a fire pit and lawn games. We also serve signature Blue Mountain food from our food truck from April through November. Join us on the quiet end of Nelson County between Charlottesville and Lynchburg and relax in the very special setting of Blue Mountain Barrel House.[/vc_column_text][divider line_type="No Line" Tastings feature 6 ciders on draft: 2 draft ciders are free of charge, with a small additional charge for a tasting flight of the other 4 draft ciders. Miles: 2.6 Difficulty Level: Moderate
A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. Miles: 2.6 Difficulty Level: Moderate
A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. Miles: 2.6 Difficulty Level: Moderate
A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. text_direction="default"][/split_line_heading][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Crabtree Falls features a series of five major cascades and a number of smaller ones that fall a total distance of 1,200 feet. The first overlook is just a few hundred feet from the parking lot along a gentle, paved trail making it an excellent stopover for travelers of all ages and abilities. The more adventuresome hiker may continue along the 3-mile trail to four other overlooks offering spectacular views of the Crabtree Creek Falls and lovely vistas of the Tye River Valley. From the upper falls, the trail follows the creek another 1.2 miles to the Crabtree Meadows. Please stay on trail – rocks are slippery. Open dawn to dusk. Parking lot with daily parking fee per vehicle. All dogs must be leashed. Directions From US Route 29, take Route 56 west at Colleen. Follow Rt. 56 for approximately 20 miles to 11581 Crabtree Falls Highway, Montebello, VA. From the Blue Ridge Parkway (Milepost 27) take Rt. 56 east for 6.3 miles to Crabtree Falls. Address 11581 Crabtree Falls Highway, Montebello, VA 24464 (NOTE: GPS/ Navigation devices often do not work in this area.) text_direction="default"]Please visit the U.S. Forest Service Glenwood Pedlar Ranger District website for current conditions.
Address 11581 Crabtree Falls Highway (Rt 56), Montebello, VA 24464
Fees $3.00 Fee per vehicle per day. (Honor system / no change available)
Open Open Daily (dawn to dusk)
Difficulty Moderate difficulty, also some stairs on trail (most overlooks during first half of hike)
Restrictions CAUTION: Leaving the trail has resulted in numerous fatalities due to extraordinarily slippery conditions created by clear algae on rocks. Hikers must STAY ON THE TRAIL and pets must be leashed at all times. Alcoholic beverages prohibited. No horses or bicycles allowed.
Water Volume (Avg) 50 cubic feet of water per second, and eventually flows into the Tye River
Closest Town Montebello, VA
Water No drinking water available (bring water & food with you)
Hiking Prep Wear appropriate footwear/hiking shoes or other. (Opt. hiking poles)
Restrooms Vault toilets at parking lot.(Vault toilets at Crabtree Meadows (at top) are open mid-March thru end of November.
Other Amenities Picnic table(s) located near the footbridge across the parking lot.
Operated By Glenwood and Pedlar Ranger Districts: 540-291-2188 (George Washington National Forest)
Additional Info Nelson County Visitor Center (434) 263-7015 | Open Daily 9-5
[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Extra-Color-1" heading_tag="h3" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="Trail Description"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]From the end of the parking area, follow the paved trail 700 ft. to the bottom of the lower-most falls. (this first overlook is accessible for wheelchair users) At this point the trail becomes dirt, and does the first of nine switchbacks on its way to the top of the highest set of falls. The traill is well maintained, and has wooden guardrails along its steeper portions, as well as railed overlooks at the most scenic points. Arrive at the top of the falls and cross over a wooden bridge to an overlook. From here you can get a nice view of the Tye River Valley and Blue Ridge Mountains. Don’t be tempted to climb over the stone wall onto the uppermost portion of the falls. The rocks are covered with a very slippery “clear” algae, and according to the Forestry Service sign, over 30 people have fallen to their deaths climbing out onto the rocks. From this point re-cross the footbridge and either head back down, or continue left up the trail where the hike becomes much flatter and follows Crabtree Stream. If you continue upwards, the trail will split in 70 yards. Take the right fork uphill as it first traverses the ridge, then follows the stream to the upper parking area in 1.1 miles. (Crabtree Meadows) To return, retrace your steps back down. Or, from the upper trailhead parking lot, continue to the left on FDR-263/VA 826 to access the Appalachian Trail just a short distance further (The AT crosses the road in 0.7 miles). Excerpted in part from HikingUpward.com[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Extra-Color-1" heading_tag="h3" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="Directions"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]From I-81: Take exit 205 for Raphine/Steeles Tavern and continue east on State Route (SR) 606 to US 11. Turn left onto US 11 and continue north for a very short distance, then take a right onto SR 56. Follow SR 56 for 2 miles into the community of Vesuvius. As you enter Vesuvius, continue on the road as it bears to the left for another 6 miles. At the top of the mountain, continue under the Blue Ridge Parkway on SR 56 for 6 to 8 miles. The entrance to Crabtree Falls Day Use Area is on the right. From the Blue Ridge Parkway (Milepost 27): Take Route 56 East for 6.3 miles to Crabtree Falls Day Use Area on your right. From US Route 29: Take Route 56 West at Colleen, follow Route 56 West for approximately 20 miles to Crabtree Falls Day Use Area on your left. (Next left after Crabtree Falls Campground – about ½ mile). Alternative way to Access Upper Crabtree Falls Trailhead at Crabtree Meadows: To explore the “top of the falls” one can take Forest Road 826 off of Rt. 56 (West of the Crabtree Falls Day Use area). This road leads to Crabtree Meadows and the Upper Trail Head. Recommended for four-wheel vehicles only, this road is rough and challenging. There are three places where you may have to cross water on the road, and one can come across fallen trees, branches or large rocks, and vehicles with little clearance underneath may scrape bottom. You’ll see a few campsites on the way up on each side of the road, and once you’re at the upper parking area it will be easy to see the trail head leading to the falls. (Parking area has trashcans and a vault toilet.) It’s 1.1 miles from Crabtree Meadows to the top of the falls. The trail continues down the falls about 2.6 miles to the lower trail head and parking area. Crabtree Meadows is an open area with crab apples and apple trees, across the road from the parking lot. In the 1930’s, several families lived in this area, which once included a saw mill. Now it is a popular primitive camping spot, with access to the Appalachian Trail which is only 0.7 miles from the parking lot up the steep gravel fire road (FDR-263/VA-823). The fall colors at Crabtree Meadows, in particular, can be spectacular![/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Extra-Color-1" heading_tag="h3" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="History"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]The name “Crabtree” is thought to have come from William Crabtree, who settled in the area in 1777. Another noted pioneer, Allen Tye, who did extensive exploration in the Blue Ridge Mountains, is identified as having discovered the Tye River. To add to its popularity, Crabtree Falls was sometimes referred to as a Sunday outing location in the 1970’s television show, “The Waltons.” The land at the base of the falls was almost developed as a resort area in the late 1960s. LA Snead, former US Assistant Fuel Administrator (WWI), environmentalist and notable Nelsonian, blocked development efforts and spearheaded negotiations to secure the land surrounding the falls. Using personal and Congressional funds, the land deals were completed and the deeds transferred by LA Snead on June 3, 1968 to the National Forest System. This assured benefit for future generations of this magnificent Nelson County treasure. Under National Forest domain, the safety, accessibility and continued improvements have made Crabtree Falls a major tourist destination within Nelson County. There are wooden stairs, gravel paths, railed overlooks, and a spectacular 100-foot bridge over the Tye River. This beautiful bridge, a laminated arch, was shipped from New York in one piece and installed over the Tye River in 1978. Until the mid-1980’s, the footbridge was the starting point for the hike up Crabtree Falls. Today the parking area is on the other side of the river, and the bridge now serves primarily as a decorative addition to the hike.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Extra-Color-1" heading_tag="h3" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="Nearby Attractions"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Montebello Fish Hatchery (0.6 miles on Rt. 56 West) 359 Fish Hatchery Lane, Montebello, VA 24464 540-377-2418 Montebello Country Store and Café (4.5 miles on Rt. 56 West) 15072 Crabtree Falls Highway, Montebello, VA 24464 540-377-2650 Montebello Camping & Fishing Resort (4.5 miles on Rt. 56 West) 15072 Crabtree Falls Highway, Montebello, VA 24464 540-377-2650[/vc_column_text][/toggle][/toggles][/vc_column][/vc_row]

text_direction="default"][/split_line_heading][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Crabtree Falls features a series of five major cascades and a number of smaller ones that fall a total distance of 1,200 feet. The first overlook is just a few hundred feet from the parking lot along a gentle, paved trail making it an excellent stopover for travelers of all ages and abilities. The more adventuresome hiker may continue along the 3-mile trail to four other overlooks offering spectacular views of the Crabtree Creek Falls and lovely vistas of the Tye River Valley. From the upper falls, the trail follows the creek another 1.2 miles to the Crabtree Meadows. Please stay on trail – rocks are slippery. Open dawn to dusk. Parking lot with daily parking fee per vehicle. All dogs must be leashed. Directions From US Route 29, take Route 56 west at Colleen. Follow Rt. 56 for approximately 20 miles to 11581 Crabtree Falls Highway, Montebello, VA. From the Blue Ridge Parkway (Milepost 27) take Rt. 56 east for 6.3 miles to Crabtree Falls. Address 11581 Crabtree Falls Highway, Montebello, VA 24464 (NOTE: GPS/ Navigation devices often do not work in this area.) text_direction="default"]Please visit the U.S. Forest Service Glenwood Pedlar Ranger District website for current conditions.
Address 11581 Crabtree Falls Highway (Rt 56), Montebello, VA 24464
Fees $3.00 Fee per vehicle per day. (Honor system / no change available)
Open Open Daily (dawn to dusk)
Difficulty Moderate difficulty, also some stairs on trail (most overlooks during first half of hike)
Restrictions CAUTION: Leaving the trail has resulted in numerous fatalities due to extraordinarily slippery conditions created by clear algae on rocks. Hikers must STAY ON THE TRAIL and pets must be leashed at all times. Alcoholic beverages prohibited. No horses or bicycles allowed.
Water Volume (Avg) 50 cubic feet of water per second, and eventually flows into the Tye River
Closest Town Montebello, VA
Water No drinking water available (bring water & food with you)
Hiking Prep Wear appropriate footwear/hiking shoes or other. (Opt. hiking poles)
Restrooms Vault toilets at parking lot.(Vault toilets at Crabtree Meadows (at top) are open mid-March thru end of November.
Other Amenities Picnic table(s) located near the footbridge across the parking lot.
Operated By Glenwood and Pedlar Ranger Districts: 540-291-2188 (George Washington National Forest)
Additional Info Nelson County Visitor Center (434) 263-7015 | Open Daily 9-5
[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Extra-Color-1" heading_tag="h3" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="Trail Description"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]From the end of the parking area, follow the paved trail 700 ft. to the bottom of the lower-most falls. (this first overlook is accessible for wheelchair users) At this point the trail becomes dirt, and does the first of nine switchbacks on its way to the top of the highest set of falls. The traill is well maintained, and has wooden guardrails along its steeper portions, as well as railed overlooks at the most scenic points. Arrive at the top of the falls and cross over a wooden bridge to an overlook. From here you can get a nice view of the Tye River Valley and Blue Ridge Mountains. Don’t be tempted to climb over the stone wall onto the uppermost portion of the falls. The rocks are covered with a very slippery “clear” algae, and according to the Forestry Service sign, over 30 people have fallen to their deaths climbing out onto the rocks. From this point re-cross the footbridge and either head back down, or continue left up the trail where the hike becomes much flatter and follows Crabtree Stream. If you continue upwards, the trail will split in 70 yards. Take the right fork uphill as it first traverses the ridge, then follows the stream to the upper parking area in 1.1 miles. (Crabtree Meadows) To return, retrace your steps back down. Or, from the upper trailhead parking lot, continue to the left on FDR-263/VA 826 to access the Appalachian Trail just a short distance further (The AT crosses the road in 0.7 miles). Excerpted in part from HikingUpward.com[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Extra-Color-1" heading_tag="h3" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="Directions"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]From I-81: Take exit 205 for Raphine/Steeles Tavern and continue east on State Route (SR) 606 to US 11. Turn left onto US 11 and continue north for a very short distance, then take a right onto SR 56. Follow SR 56 for 2 miles into the community of Vesuvius. As you enter Vesuvius, continue on the road as it bears to the left for another 6 miles. At the top of the mountain, continue under the Blue Ridge Parkway on SR 56 for 6 to 8 miles. The entrance to Crabtree Falls Day Use Area is on the right. From the Blue Ridge Parkway (Milepost 27): Take Route 56 East for 6.3 miles to Crabtree Falls Day Use Area on your right. From US Route 29: Take Route 56 West at Colleen, follow Route 56 West for approximately 20 miles to Crabtree Falls Day Use Area on your left. (Next left after Crabtree Falls Campground – about ½ mile). Alternative way to Access Upper Crabtree Falls Trailhead at Crabtree Meadows: To explore the “top of the falls” one can take Forest Road 826 off of Rt. 56 (West of the Crabtree Falls Day Use area). This road leads to Crabtree Meadows and the Upper Trail Head. Recommended for four-wheel vehicles only, this road is rough and challenging. There are three places where you may have to cross water on the road, and one can come across fallen trees, branches or large rocks, and vehicles with little clearance underneath may scrape bottom. You’ll see a few campsites on the way up on each side of the road, and once you’re at the upper parking area it will be easy to see the trail head leading to the falls. (Parking area has trashcans and a vault toilet.) It’s 1.1 miles from Crabtree Meadows to the top of the falls. The trail continues down the falls about 2.6 miles to the lower trail head and parking area. Crabtree Meadows is an open area with crab apples and apple trees, across the road from the parking lot. In the 1930’s, several families lived in this area, which once included a saw mill. Now it is a popular primitive camping spot, with access to the Appalachian Trail which is only 0.7 miles from the parking lot up the steep gravel fire road (FDR-263/VA-823). The fall colors at Crabtree Meadows, in particular, can be spectacular![/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Extra-Color-1" heading_tag="h3" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="History"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]The name “Crabtree” is thought to have come from William Crabtree, who settled in the area in 1777. Another noted pioneer, Allen Tye, who did extensive exploration in the Blue Ridge Mountains, is identified as having discovered the Tye River. To add to its popularity, Crabtree Falls was sometimes referred to as a Sunday outing location in the 1970’s television show, “The Waltons.” The land at the base of the falls was almost developed as a resort area in the late 1960s. LA Snead, former US Assistant Fuel Administrator (WWI), environmentalist and notable Nelsonian, blocked development efforts and spearheaded negotiations to secure the land surrounding the falls. Using personal and Congressional funds, the land deals were completed and the deeds transferred by LA Snead on June 3, 1968 to the National Forest System. This assured benefit for future generations of this magnificent Nelson County treasure. Under National Forest domain, the safety, accessibility and continued improvements have made Crabtree Falls a major tourist destination within Nelson County. There are wooden stairs, gravel paths, railed overlooks, and a spectacular 100-foot bridge over the Tye River. This beautiful bridge, a laminated arch, was shipped from New York in one piece and installed over the Tye River in 1978. Until the mid-1980’s, the footbridge was the starting point for the hike up Crabtree Falls. Today the parking area is on the other side of the river, and the bridge now serves primarily as a decorative addition to the hike.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Extra-Color-1" heading_tag="h3" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="Nearby Attractions"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Montebello Fish Hatchery (0.6 miles on Rt. 56 West) 359 Fish Hatchery Lane, Montebello, VA 24464 540-377-2418 Montebello Country Store and Café (4.5 miles on Rt. 56 West) 15072 Crabtree Falls Highway, Montebello, VA 24464 540-377-2650 Montebello Camping & Fishing Resort (4.5 miles on Rt. 56 West) 15072 Crabtree Falls Highway, Montebello, VA 24464 540-377-2650[/vc_column_text][/toggle][/toggles][/vc_column][/vc_row]

Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. text_direction="default"][/split_line_heading][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Miles: 5.3 Difficulty Level: Difficult Fortune’s Cove provides two loops that reward visitors with stunning mountain vistas. The preserve is situated within some 29,000 acres of relatively intact forest habitat and hosts rare plant communities on a series of rocky glades. The 5.3-mile loop trail climbs steeply from the parking area, gaining some 1,500 feet in elevation before reaching its highest point. The trail forks at the 0.8-mile mark. Continuing along the Upper Loop (Yellow Trail) makes for an arduous 5.1-mile counter-clockwise trek around the horseshoe-shaped cove. Hikers should be in good physical condition and should allow about four hours to complete this trail. Turning left at the fork onto the Lower Loop (or White Trail) shortens the total distance to 3.7 miles and lowers the intensity by cutting out the steepest climbs. A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. Hiking Humpback Rocks is a relatively short moderate hike following a 2.0-mile (3.2 km) trail loop. With a roughly 45 minute hike to ascend 740 feet (230 m) to the peak, and a 20-25 minute descent, this ranks as one of the shorter hikes along the Blue Ridge, however it remains one of the most rewarding. The peak affords a spectacular 360 degree view of the surrounding terrain. To the north you can see into the southern section of Shenandoah National Park, to the east check out the patchwork of farms, to the southwest you see thick woods and mountain ridges of the George Washington National Forest. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. This section of the Appalachian Trail, combined with the other trail in the wilderness, the three mile long Mau-Har Trail, creates “one of the best loop trails in the state of Virginia,” according to one guidebook.These trails are maintained by the Tidewater Appalachian Trail Club, a trail maintenance club affiliated with the Appalachian Trail Conservancy. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. Miles: 2.6 Difficulty Level: Moderate
A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. The road is recommended for travel only by higher clearance, four-wheel drive vehicles. Access to the trail requires a minimum 6.5-mile round-trip hike which includes a steady uphill grade, sections of very steep trail and rocky terrain and sections of gravel road.   • From State Route 56, take State Route 826 (Meadows Lane) for approximately 3.75 miles to its end point at the Crabtree Meadows parking area.
  • From the Crabtree Meadows parking area, hike back along State Route 826 for 0.5 miles and turn left onto Forest Service Road 596 (Cash Hollow Road).
  • Hike* along Forest Service Road 596 (Cash Hollow Road) for 0.5 miles to the intersection with the Appalachian Trail.
  • Turn right (south) on the Appalachian Trail and continue for 2.1 miles to the intersection with Spy Rock Trail, Forest Trail #732.

A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. Miles: 2.6 Difficulty Level: Moderate
A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. riding year round. The main trailhead is in Piney River on SR 151, Patrick Henry Hwy. It has ample parking for cars and horse trailers. A smaller trail head (at milepost 1.7) in Roses Mill on SR 674, Roses Mill Rd can accommodate only cars. Restroom facilities are available at both trail heads. The mainly crushed stone trail follows a scenic route along the Piney and Tye Rivers, where wildflowers bloom from spring through summer and wildlife abounds. The trail dead ends at the 7 mile point, there is no eastern access at Tye River Depot, so you must retrace your steps to your vehicle. During the autumn hunting season, trail users should wear blaze orange clothing. The trail is open sunrise to sunset. The trail occupies the rail bed of the former Virginia Blue Ridge Railway, which ran from Tye River Depot (to interchange with the Southern Railway) to Massies Mill. Construction of the railroad started in 1915 and the line was abandoned in 1980. Address 3124 Patrick Henry Highway Piney River, Virginia, 22964 Parking and Trail Access To access the Piney River trailhead from the Lovingston area, take US 29 to State Route 56 west at Colleen; turn right onto SR 56, and travel 5 miles to turn left onto SR 151. After 2 miles you’ll see the trailhead sign on left (3124 Patrick Henry Highway, Piney River). Parking for cars and horse trailers is available. To access the Roses Mill trailhead from the Lovingston area, take US 29 to SR 56 west at Colleen; turn right onto SR 56 and go about 4 miles to left turn onto Roses Mill Road/SR 674). The main trailhead is in Piney River on SR 151, Patrick Henry Hwy. It has ample parking for cars and horse trailers. The mainly crushed stone trail follows a scenic route along the Piney and Tye Rivers, where wildflowers bloom from spring through summer and wildlife abounds. The trail dead ends at the 7 mile point, there is no eastern access at Tye River Depot, so you must retrace your steps to your vehicle. During the autumn hunting season, trail users should wear blaze orange clothing. The trail is open sunrise to sunset. The trail occupies the rail bed of the former Virginia Blue Ridge Railway, which ran from Tye River Depot (to interchange with the Southern Railway) to Massies Mill. Construction of the railroad started in 1915 and the line was abandoned in 1980. After 2 miles you’ll see the trailhead sign on left (3124 Patrick Henry Highway, Piney River). Parking for cars and horse trailers is available. To access the Roses Mill trailhead from the Lovingston area, take US 29 to SR 56 west at Colleen; turn right onto SR 56 and go about 4 miles to left turn onto Roses Mill Road/SR 674). Outboard motor use is prohibited but electric motors are permitted. 801 Lake Nelson Lane Arrington, VA 22922 434-263-7015 Directions Lake Nelson can be accessed from Route 29 near Colleen (Nelson County), then take Route 655 about 2.8 miles to Arrington; go through Arrington, then left on Route 812, go about 2.2 miles and watch for the sign. border_radius="none"][toggle color="Accent-Color" heading_tag="h3" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="James River (Upper and Middle)"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]From the confluence of the Jackson and Cowpasture Rivers in Botetourt County, downstream to Richmond, the James River offers a wide range of angling opportunities and settings. Smallmouth bass are the dominant game species, but spotted and largemouth bass can also be caught. Smallmouth bass fishing can be good throughout the river. Both the mountain sections (upstream from Lynchburg) and the piedmont sections (between Lynchburg and Richmond) generally provide good fishing. Other species are also plentiful in the James River, including channel catfish, flathead catfish, and various sunfish species (redbreast, bluegill, and rock bass). Flathead catfish appear to be more numerous upstream from Lynchburg, and channel catfish are more numerous below Lynchburg. Muskies are also annually stocked in the James. These fish are scarce, but some very large fish can be caught. Most of the muskies are found upstream from Lynchburg. Overall, the James River offers an excellent fishing opportunity for whatever you might want. Canoeing is the best way to access the river. Small boats (such as john boats) can also be used at most access points. Bank and wade fishing access is also available throughout the river. Virginia Fishing License(s) are required.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Accent-Color" heading_tag="h3" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="James River (Wildlife Management Area)"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]The area fronts one of the better stretches of the James River for fishing. Anglers land smallmouth bass, various sunfishes and channel catfish. This section of the river is popular for float fishing. A one-acre pond provides a variety of sunfish for those — perhaps with young anglers — not interested in fishing the river. The ramp access makes the area an excellent “put in” or “take out” point for James River canoeists. For fishermen, a number of trout stocked streams are nearby, west of the management area in Nelson County. A boat launching ramp provides year-round access to the James River. The area is located approximately 15 miles south-east of Lovingston in the southeastern portion of Nelson County, near the community of Wingina. Access is from State Route 56, between Lovingston and Buckingham Court House, on Route 626 travel easterly following road signs. The Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources requires an Access Permit for visitors to department-owned Wildlife Management Areas (WMAs) and public fishing lakes effective January 1, 2012, who are age 17 and older, unless they possess a valid Virginia hunting, freshwater fishing, or trapping license, or a current Virginia boat registration.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Accent-Color" heading_tag="h3" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="James River State Park"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]One of Virginia’s newest state parks, James River State Park has 1,500 acres with three ponds for fishing: Branch Pond, Green Hill Pond and Taylor Pond in addition to freshwater fishing on the James River. Where fishing is permitted, valid Virginia fishing licenses are required. Specific licenses are required for saltwater and trout-water fishing. Please call the park in advance for specifics. Facilities available at this reservoir are a boat ramp, parking area and portable toilets which are available March-September. Fishermen are likely to catch largemouth bass, channel catfish, black crappie, bluegill, and redear sunfish. The lake is open 24 hours a day. Wintergreen’s Orvis-Endorsed instructors have the perfect classroom setting at Lake Monocan to introduce students to the art of Fly Fishing, or anglers can experience the thrill of fishing for trout in the mountains or smallmouth bass on the legendary James River with a knowledgeable and friendly guide. text_content="The Details" font_size="3vw" text_direction="default"][/split_line_heading][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]When Ellis Maples designed this 18 hole gem, the highest golf course in Virginia, his challenge was to enhance its stunning Blue Ridge Mountain setting. Sitting at an elevation of over 3,800 feet, players leave Devils Knob Golf Course remembering narrow fairways, excellent turf conditions and unsurpassed vistas. Typically 12-18 degrees cooler even than its sister golf course, Stoney Creek, Devils Knob provides Virginia’s coolest playing conditions throughout the summer and the most dramatic mountain foliage backdrop throughout the fall. If you are searching for a true mountain golf challenge, Devils Knob golf course is a “must play.”
  • At 3,850 feet, the highest course in the State of Virginia
  • Access is only available to members, guests and registered resort guests
  • 50-mile views of the Shenandoah and Rockfish valleys
  • Surprisingly level mountaintop terrain
  • Pleasant 70-85 degree temperatures throughout the spring and summer
  • Spacious 16,585 square foot clubhouse, featuring pro shop with top-of-the-line merchandise, locker room, fine dining and snack shop.

Miles: 2.6 Difficulty Level: Moderate
A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. A 2.6-mile moderate hike along the Appalachian Trail traverses a wooden Swinging Bridge over the Tye River, and travels through stands of mountain laurel and rhododendron to the Harpers Creek Shelter (AT) and Harper’s Creek, where the water gurgles through the large cascading rocks. Multiple campsites are on each side of the creek, and there’s a vault toilet up the hill from the shelter. Directions From State Route 56 at Crabtree Falls: Take SR 56 east for approximately 3-4 miles. The Appalachian Trail crosses SR 56 and a AT parking lot is available to the right (South side) of SR 56. Head across the street from the parking lot (North) on the AT across the Swinging Bridge, and continue up the trail towards Harper’s Creek Shelter. Wintergreen Resort
Wintergreen Resort has facilities for indoor and outdoor swimming with indoor facilities available year-round. Lake Monocan Park at Stoney Creek Swimming at Lake Monocan is available from Memorial Day Weekend through Labor Day. Members and all registered resort guests have complimentary access to Lake Monocan Park. Swimming at Lake Monocan is open to the public every day except Saturday, when only Wintergreen Resort members and guests are allowed. A fee is charged for non-guests using the Monocan Park facilities. Swimming Pools at Wintergreen Resort The Wintergarden Spa and Fitness Center indoor pool is open year-round. All Wintergreen outdoor pools are open daily from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day. Outdoor pools are located at the Aquatics & Fitness Center and Stoney Creek Golf Course. For more information on pools call 434-325-8280. Website
River Swimming
Swimming in the rivers of Nelson County can be fun and offer very different experiences. From the mighty James River that borders on the eastern side of the county to the mountain streams that include, Piney River, Tye River and Rockfish River offer many opportunities to enjoy the water. Permission must be obtained when accessing these streams on private property.[/vc_column_text][nectar_btn size="jumbo" button_style="regular" button_color_2="Extra-Color-3" icon_family="none" text="See More Ways to Play" url="/play" margin_top="10" margin_bottom="10"][/vc_column][/vc_row]

families since its construction in 1794, when Guiliford Campbell built the original four-story, 32 foot square building. The Fulchers improved it in the 1840’s, adding the two runs (mill stones), which are still in use today. Sixty-some years later, Dr. Julian B. Woodson expanded the mill into a thriving enterprise that included an icehouse, sawmill, and foundry while maintaining his duties as a medical doctor and State Senator. The rise of large industrial mills in the growing post-war America, along with Dr. Woodson’s death in 1963, brought a temporary end to the mill business. But, Huron T. Campbell, who owned the mill while it was not in operation, refused to sell any of the equipment or machinery in hope that someone would eventually be able to restore it. J. Gill Brockenbrough, Jr., who purchased Woodson’s Mill in the early 1980’s, did restore it and lived there until his death in 2001. Four of the breweries are in Nelson County along scenic Route 151; Starr Hill is in nearby Crozet, and South Street Brewery is in Charlottesville.

The self-guided tour allows you to check out all of our breweries at your leisure. Each brewery offers Sample Tastings of their craft beers, allowing you to try out a variety of what they produce. The kitchen is fully stocked with everything you need to cook and serve your family. There is a coffee/tea bar as well as a counter top ice maker. There is a private bedroom with a queen size bed on the main level. Upstairs in the loft you will find three sleeping areas. The first area has 2 queen size beds, the second area has 2 twin size beds, and the third area has a full size bed with a private balcony over looking the pond. Back downstairs is the single bathroom which also has a full size washer and dryer. Outside you will find a deck that wraps around 2 sides of the house. Featuring a hot tub large enough for the whole crew, many seating areas, outdoor dining, propane and charcoal grills, as well as covered areas. Grab a chair and have a seat next to the private pond. Throw in a fishing line if you brought any along, and maybe have a fire in the fire pit if you are feeling like having s'mores. Title: Retreat at Crabtree Falls
Content: The Retreat at Crabtree Falls offers a distinctive lodging experience in Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains. This property offers numerous accommodations which each feature a spacious layout with bedrooms, a fully equipped kitchen, and a comfortable living area, providing guests with a home-like atmosphere amidst nature. What sets The Retreat apart is its proximity to the stunning Crabtree Falls, the highest vertical-drop cascading waterfall east of the Mississippi River. Guests can easily access the falls and enjoy the surrounding hiking trails, immersing themselves in the natural beauty of the area. The Retreat's secluded location offers tranquility and privacy, making it an ideal choice for families, couples, or groups seeking a peaceful getaway. Modern amenities, combined with the rustic charm of the mountains, ensure a comfortable and memorable stay at The Retreat at Crabtree Falls. At The Retreat at Crabtree Falls, our dedicated staff is committed to ensuring your stay is both luxurious and memorable. We take pride in maintaining impeccably clean accommodations, providing a pristine environment for your comfort. Our team is always on hand, ready to respond promptly to your needs and assist in crafting the perfect vacation experience. Whether it's arranging local excursions, offering personalized recommendations, or attending to special requests, we are here to make your stay exceptional.

Whether you are looking for a peaceful weekend getaway, or an active family reunion, enjoy resort living at its best in this completely renovated home with breathtaking mountain views and a one-of-a-kind huge fenced-in yard, perfect for entertaining large groups, kids and dogs. With two separate entertaining areas, our house can accommodate lots of fun and games. The first floor great room provides a huge sectional sofa (with queen pullout bed), large flat screen tv, a pool table (with ping pong table topper), a foosball table, and a big table perfect for playing games or doing puzzles...and opens to an expansive porch and huge hot tub that seats seven. The hot tub is the perfect place to view the night ski and beautiful stars. Upstairs, you will find a large, open-plan living area that provides amazing two-story views of the mountains. The HDTV and extensive, comfortable seating provides a great place to watch a movie or sporting event, and the magnificent stone fireplace is perfect for roasting marshmallows or warming up after a long day of skiing. The house is fully stocked with games, puzzles and movies galore for hours of entertainment. And enjoy the outdoors while relaxing on the many seating opportunities provided on the two-story deck. The expansive high-end chef's kitchen includes tons of storage and unique countertops (made from recycled paper!), an induction cooktop, wall oven, microwave, refrigerator/freezer, beverage fridge, two sinks, two dishwashers (for easy clean up!) and direct access to the gas grill on the connecting porch. Your guests can enjoy your meals at the nearby large dining table that seats 10 (12 with extra seats!) or from the large kitchen island that seats 4. The five bedrooms all feature gorgeous beds and gracious bathrooms. The master bedroom, located on the second floor, is our presidential suite, featuring a gas fireplace, large hdtv, two sitting areas and sliding glass doors which open for cool mountain breezes and the most amazing views of the mountains at sunrise. The master bathroom offers a beautifully tiled shower and jetted tub, where you can relax, look at the mountains from the private bathroom window, or enjoy your favorite show on the flat screen tv. The four bedrooms downstairs include a guest master bedroom with queen bed and HDTV, and a huge, beautifully tiled shower; a guest room with double bed and attached bathroom with tub/shower combo; and, two fun bunk rooms, each with their own bathrooms. Additional sleeping options are available on the queen pull out sleeper sofa.   • A perfect location. Based in the heart of the Nelson 151 Craft Beverage Trail and a short drive from the Blue Ridge Parkway and Shenandoah National Park, you're well-positioned for days of exploration!

This home sleeps up to 16 guests and provides entertainment for all ages. The main level includes a fully equipped kitchen, dining room, cozy living room, and a primary bedroom (King bed) with an ensuite bath. Large A-Frame windows allow the sunlight to come through so you can enjoy the birds and nature all around. The property sits on 3.5 acres so it is very private. An expansive rolling lawn in the front to enjoy watching the deer in the morning while having a cup of coffee on the wide front porch. Forest areas on the side and back of the house. Enter the home in the front door and a warm and welcoming living room await you with two couches and a gas burning fireplace. Throw blankets and pillows for snuggling while watching a movie. TV and DVD player with a selection of movies to choose from. The dining room with bay seated window has a large table to seat 6 comfortably. The front porch also has a dining table. Spacious, well appointed kitchen with all you need for preparing delicious meals after a day of hiking the Appalachian trail or sightseeing. Dish-ware, flatware, sauce and saute pans. Wine glasses, coffee mugs, serving ware. Crock pot, blender, mixer. Coffee pot with coffee bean grinder (Starbucks coffee beans in the pantry). You will find a few condiments in the refrigerator, spices, herbs, oil in the pantry. The loft bedroom has a Queen bed and a Double Bed with a private bathroom and shower. The first floor bedroom has two twin beds and a separate bathroom with walk in shower. Loft area also has a desk with laptop and printer for your use. text_direction="default"]Experience the Blue Ridge Mountains and country life of central Virginia and enjoy everything Nelson County has to offer. The Cottage on the Knoll is a comfortable 3br/2bth that’s centrally located in Nelson County, offering the perfect mix of modern comfort and country charm. The Nelson 29 and Nelson 151 craft beverage trails await you, while plenty of hiking, fishing, and mountain views will appease any outdoor recreation lover or nature enthusiast, making it the perfect getaway. The space: This three bedroom / two bathroom home features a bright and comfortable main area that includes a large kitchen area and living space that is fully stocked with all amenities. Adjacent to the main living area are two bedrooms featuring queen beds and a full bathroom. A large recreation room downstairs includes a ping pong table, a selection of board games, a mounted TV, and extra seating for fun nights in. The third bedroom with king sized bed and full bath is located downstairs beside the recreation room. After a day in the mountains, cook a meal in your fully stocked kitchen and kick back and enjoy your evenings outside, where you’ll find a wood fire pit in the yard and a gas fireplace and hot tub on the large covered porch. High-speed internet and a smart TV with limited channel access will allow you to connect to your own streaming accounts. Private in-ground swimming pool is available for cottage guests and apartment guests to use during your stay. We will gladly heat the pool during your visit for an additional cost of $25 per day during cooler months. Please indicate if you would like to have the pool heated during your stay at the time of booking so the costs can be adjusted. ** Please note the pool could meet the max number of 8 people if both rentals use it at the same time ** If you would like the pool to yourself during your stay, reach out for additional cost and availability.[/vc_column_text][split_line_heading animation_type="line-reveal-by-space" font_style="h6" text_color="#50623a" line_reveal_by_space_text_effect="none" content_alignment="default" mobile_content_alignment="center" link_target="_self" text_content="What Makes This Space Unique" font_size="3vw" text_direction="default"][/split_line_heading][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Whole house centrally located with private hot tub and pool. 30 min away from Charlottesville, Lynchburg, Waynesboro and the top of Wintergreen Resort. css="" text_direction="default"]Glenbrae is located just off the iconic Nelson 151 and 1 mile from Afton Mountain Vineyards. This property was stylishly decorated by a local interior designer and is the perfect getaway for a group of friends, family, or couples traveling together. Along with its 5 spacious bedrooms, large living area, and Peloton, this property also has beautiful mountain views. Halfway between Wintergreen and Charlottesville you can be at either in under 30 min. NEW fully fenced backyard over 1/2 acre - perfect for your pups and kids to run around! MAIN FLOOR: OFFICE - Peloton (cages provided - just bring your sneakers and you won't have to clip in!), desk, office chair, bookshelves, two chairs for additional seating. BEDROOM 1 - Queen bed, bench, sconce lights with charging ports, side tables, smart TV, and closet with hangers. DINING ROOM - Dining table with seating for 10, gas fireplace (currently not for guest use) KITCHEN - Full equipped kitchen will full-size appliances and pantry space, French door fridge, microwave, dishwasher, electric range and oven, bar seating for 4. LIVING ROOM - Smart TV, two sofas (seating for 6), coffee table, game table with seating for 4, arm chair, French doors with patio access. BATHROOM 1 - Full bathroom with tub/shower combo. OUTDOOR - Fenced in yard and firepit. UPSTAIRS: BEDROOM 2 - King bed, Smart TV, side tables, hanging bedside lights, mirror, console table with drawers, and closet with hangers. BATHROOM 2 - Full bathroom with tub/shower combo. BEDROOM 3 - Queen bed, side tables, sconces on each side of bed, chair, mirror, and closet with hangers. BEDROOM 4 - 2 twin beds, side table and lamp, and closet with hangers. BEDROOM 5 (MASTER) - King bed, desk/vanity with chair and mirror, smart TV, side tables with lamps, loveseat, and walk-in closet with hangers. css="" text_direction="default"]Mountaintop overlook with jaw dropping views and camp themed interior design. Perched upon Elk Mountain just off the Blue Ridge Parkway this petite chalet is under 30 min from Charlottesville, 10 min to 151 vineyards/breweries/cideries, and 10 min to Waynesboro. Relax in this natural retreat featuring 2 king bedrooms, 2 person soaker tub, double headed shower, and ample kitchen w/many extras. Take in the views from the large deck, firepit, under porch swing, or mountainside adirondack chairs. Primarily one level home with sleeping loft. Main floor consists of open concept kitchen, dining, living with electric fireplace. Full bathroom with dual head shower has jack and jill access off the hallway and primary bedroom. Main floor primary bedroom has king bed, walk in closet, and large soaker tub. Laundry is located in the primary bedroom. Upstairs there is a sleeping loft with another king bed. Deck is on the back of the house accessed from the main living/dining areas. From the deck you can see Afton Mountain Vineyard, Veritas, Blue Mountain Brewery, Hazy Mountain and even across to Mont Alto on a clear day. There are approximately 4 steps to get into the front door from the gravel driveway. The one Roku TV is located in the living room. This property was designed for adult guests so anyone wanting to bring children should keep in mind that the property is quite steep and the deck is high off the ground. Note- no ice maker. 4WD or AWD highly recommended in winter- all roads are paved but snow or ice can be prevalent in winter and provide a challenge to 2WD vehicles. While our private road can be accessed directly off the Blue Ridge Parkway we advise arriving via Howardsville TPK to avoid road closures. Weather should always be checked before heading up the mountain as fog can limit visibility. The house does have a generator that kicks on in case of power outage. Whether you are coming for the wine/beer hopping, a vineyard wedding (Veritas is a 3 min drive), or to get outdoors (Blueridge Tunnel Trail- 3 min, Shenandoah National Park - 15 min), Sweet Afton is perfect retreat! High speed, 1gig internet in the rural country. Sweet Afton is a historic cottage, yet recently updated with modern amenities (central heating and air, updated kitchen appliances) and tasteful new furnishings provide a fresh, relaxing and bucolic atmosphere. The plot has well maintained gardens surrounding the house and walkways, a hammock, a fire pit with 6 chairs and two porches to enjoy a morning coffee or evening glass of wine with company. Upon the entry to the cottage (enter from driveway in the rear) there is a full kitchen and all of the cooking essentials you will need.   Off of the kitchen is a spacious dining room (seats 6) with large bay windows providing beautiful mountain views towards the southwest.  From the dining room, a central hallway leads through to the front of the house. Off the hallway, are both bedrooms (queen beds), the full bath and an inviting living room with a pull-out couch (king but also can be a double), a TV and a desk.  All of the rooms feel very spacious due to the 10 ft ceilings and natural light from the large windows. On the front of the house is a covered porch with six rocking chairs and a gas grill. Large bushes in front of the house provide privacy from the nearby road. text_direction="default"][/split_line_heading][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Devils Backbone Camp offers an unparalleled camping experience in the heart of the Blue Ridge Mountains, combining a causal camp experience with world-class craft beverages and food. With a range of sites, from full-hook-up RV to rustic wooded tent sites, we offer a range of camping options for every type of adventurer. Nestled in a 5-acre bier garden featuring yard games, numerous seating options, and seasonal live music, our Basecamp Brewpub is open daily with 16+ taps, a full bar, and a seasonal menu featuring smoked meats and something for your whole family to enjoy. In addition to our Basecamp Indoor Brewpub, we have our craft Distillery Lounge, Shanty Cigar Lounge, Summit merchandise shop & Meadows Outdoor Bar & Outdoor grill on property to enjoy as well. Centrally located in the Rockfish Valley, Devils Backbone Camp is within a short drive of some of Virginia’s best hiking, golf, and skiing. Only 5 miles to the Skyline Drive and the Reid's Gap trailhead on the Appalachian Trail, whether exploring by foot or on two wheels, you won’t find any shortage of paths or stunning views. Positioned on the "Nelson 151" route, Devils Backbone Camp is the prime home base to explore our neighboring breweries, cideries, wineries, and distilleries. With over 20 craft beverage producers within a 20-minute drive, you will find something to suit everyone's tastes. The village of Nellysford offers local dining, shopping a farmers’ market, and a day trip to Charlottesville or Staunton provides extensive shopping, dining, and cultural opportunities. text_direction="default"][/split_line_heading][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Come and enjoy a stylish European village nestled in the heart of the Blue Ridge Mountains between the scenic Blue Ridge Parkway and the Ski slopes of Wintergreen Mountain. The Inn is a one-of-a-kind hand crafted work of art that combines the classical museum quality craftsmanship with European tastes and colors and all the best modern amenities. Mastering octagons while rebuilding Poplar Forest from Jefferson’s own letters, the architect and builder of the Inn challenge the visitor to even find their way through the myriad of complex shapes, towers, curving street, and so many hidden details and works of art that it requires a return visit to take it all in. Wake to a wholesome breakfast buffet in the bakery including Belgium waffles, sausage, eggs or lighter options of fresh fruits, granola and yogurt. Take in the morning views of the National Forest as you plan your day. Hike from your room to the top of Three Ridges along the Appalachian Trail. Bike or drive on the scenic Blue Ridge Parkway, less than half mile away. In winter head up to the slopes of Wintergreen for skiing, sledding and ice skating, or in summer, enjoy a swim at Sherando Lake. All this is just minutes away. Nelson County has a number of breweries, wineries, distilleries and cideries as well as many events from music festivals to golf tournaments, cycling races, mountain bike events and professional and amateur Spartan mud races. Those interested in history can take a short drive to see Mr. Jefferson (as he is called at the University of Virginia) at Monticello in Charlottesville. His second home, Poplar Forest, is in Lynchburg. If all that sounds like too much to do, then take a slow day and unwind. Enjoy the views of the mountains from your breakfast table, stroll the main street and look for the historic tools that worked on Museums like Colonial Williamsburg, Monticello and many other museums in Virginia. Do some window shopping at our Gift store for some local crafts and brush up on your local nature and geology in our many display windows and bird watching spots. Prefer a visit to nature? Go for a short hike in the woods filled with old growth chestnut oaks, mountain laurel and tulip poplars. While you can hike for thousands of miles on the Appalachian Trail from here, a short hike from the Fenton Inn can bring you to some of the most scenic spots. Take time to look up, as this area is a migratory highway for birds of prey including bald and golden eagles and many types of hawks. Year-round residents include nesting barred owls, wild turkeys, pileated woodpeckers, ravens and smaller song birds. Return back to village life for a massage in our spa or just relax in a comfortable reading chair. The Fenton Inn is surrounded by things to do, wineries, breweries, National Parks, the Appalachian Trail and the ski slopes of Wintergreen, but the most interesting attraction in the area is a stay at the Fenton Inn. The Inn is not just a place to stay, but a must see destination for anyone interested in art, architecture and European history. Step onto the cobble stone streets and be transported back to Medieval Germany. The Inn is a complete village, with a town square, clock tower, bakery, theater, gym, spa, store and a handful of other buildings. Stroll the Main Street and window shop in the many display windows and look up at the many different half-timber facades inspired by the traditions of Bavarian timber-frame. More than just ornamental, the various braces and figures on the buildings each have historical meanings, like the Grudger head protecting from evil and envy, to the Wildman of the woods in timber bracing used in central Germany. Inside the lobby, oak timbers soar in a full arch inspired from a Medieval English church. The unit has been completely renovated inside and out including new siding, new insulation, new kitchen, new bathrooms with heated floors, all new flooring and paint throughout, new deck, and expanded parking. This house is extremely convenient to all of the amenities of Wintergreen, a Four Season resort nestled next to the Blue Ridge Parkway in Nelson County. The house is less than 1 minute from the main resort and ski lifts. You can ski in/out by walking down our rear steps and between the houses behind us on Tyro slope. No need to drive and park at the resort. There's plenty of drama in this house featuring the main floor great room with a whole house cathedral ceiling and wood stove. The completely rebuilt wrap around deck overlooks the Tyro slope and has fantastic mountain and valley views of Waynesboro and Crozet. Downstairs are 3 bedrooms all with new foam mattress beds (Queen/Queen/2 Twins) and linens. There is a cozy screen room off the master that also has mountain views. There is parking for three vehicles in the newly expanded parking pad out front, plus street parking behind the house on Tyro Lane. There are two completely remodeled full baths, one includes a stacked front load high efficiency full sized washer and dryer. The gourmet kitchen is spacious and bright and has a stove, exhaust hood, refrigerator with an ice/water dispenser, microwave, dishwasher and disposal. text_direction="default"][/split_line_heading][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Rock-n-Creek Cabin offers the comforts of country living with all modern amenities. Nestled high on the pinnacle of Whetstone Ridge in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Virginia. Conveniently located near the BRP, Appalachian Trail & Crabtree Falls. Cabin offers three covered porches and a large open deck all which overlook manicured open fields with two branches of the Tye River and a large stone fire pit. Cabin decor is eclectic with a mixture of old and new collectibles. Comfortable and romantic setting in country style. Cabin is spacious offering three private bedrooms with a semi-private sleeping loft area. Two full baths with two living areas upstairs and down. Fully equipped kitchen and plenty of outdoor setting. It’s a home away from home waiting for you.[/vc_column_text][split_line_heading animation_type="line-reveal-by-space" font_style="h6" text_color="#50623a" line_reveal_by_space_text_effect="none" content_alignment="default" mobile_content_alignment="center" link_target="_self" text_content="What Makes This Space Unique" font_size="3vw" text_direction="default"][/split_line_heading][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]There are numerous things that make Rock-n-Creek Cabin unique.  The cabin sits alone on its own property and you don’t have to share cabin or property with other guest. text_direction="default"]This 1930's Sears Roebuck home has been completed renovated to establish the modern conveniences we love yet sustain the charm we all look for in old homes. Located on 4.5 acres with views of Afton Mountain, the Blue Ridge Mountains and the vineyard hillside at Veritas. Sleeps 7 people with 3 bedrooms and 2 full bathrooms. The home features a completely open concept floor plan fit for entertaining! Gather around the 9' dining table for delicious meals made from the completely stocked kitchen that features a farmhouse sink, quartz countertops, custom cabinetry and stylish lighting to pull this rustic modern kitchen together. The conveniently located laundry room, complete with a Washer/Dryer also doubles as a pantry and coffee station. The family room is just off the entry and so cozy with two sofas and a large 64" TV to watch games and movies. Original features of the home, the built-in cabinets with antique glass doors keep the charm gleaming in this home. The first floor includes a spacious main bedroom with walk-in closet. It is equipped with a desktop for the working professional or fit for a Queen getting ready on her big day. The main level bathroom is drenched from floor to ceiling with marble tile with a restored 6' clawfoot cast iron tub that also doubles as shower. The original set of stairs leads to two more bedrooms (1 Queen and 1 Queen/1 Twin) as well as a full bathroom and landing with a workspace nook that boasts great mountain views. text_direction="default"]This 1930's Sears Roebuck home has been completed renovated to establish the modern conveniences we love yet sustain the charm we all look for in old homes. Located on 4.5 acres with views of Afton Mountain, the Blue Ridge Mountains and the vineyard hillside at Veritas. Sleeps 7 people with 3 bedrooms and 2 full bathrooms. The home features a completely open concept floor plan fit for entertaining! Gather around the 9' dining table for delicious meals made from the completely stocked kitchen that features a farmhouse sink, quartz countertops, custom cabinetry and stylish lighting to pull this rustic modern kitchen together. The conveniently located laundry room, complete with a Washer/Dryer also doubles as a pantry and coffee station. The family room is just off the entry and so cozy with two sofas and a large 64" TV to watch games and movies. Original features of the home, the built-in cabinets with antique glass doors keep the charm gleaming in this home. The first floor includes a spacious main bedroom with walk-in closet. It is equipped with a desktop for the working professional or fit for a Queen getting ready on her big day. The main level bathroom is drenched from floor to ceiling with marble tile with a restored 6' clawfoot cast iron tub that also doubles as shower. The original set of stairs leads to two more bedrooms (1 Queen and 1 Queen/1 Twin) as well as a full bathroom and landing with a workspace nook that boasts great mountain views. text_direction="default"][/split_line_heading][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]For almost 10 years Avon Hill Lodge has offered a unique getaway, close to the heart of Virginia wine country. Tucked away in the rolling hills of Nelson County, the property has served as an exclusive vacation destination and retreat for families, groups, and businesses. Located 28 miles south of Charlottesville, Avon Hill provides a serene escape with views of the Blue Ridge Mountains. The Avon Hill estate is made up of 100 tree lined acres along the Rockfish River, over five acres of English and American Boxwoods, four overnight accommodations buildings, a pool, and as of 2019, Bruce’s Barn. You're surrounded by nature at our unique eco-village cabin but also super close to the several breweries & cideries & wineries & distilleries & restaurants that Nelson County Route 151 offers. Furnishings are brand new and we've thoughtfully curated every inch of the property!! Downstairs, our chestnut leather sectional faces our large TV (65") with YouTube TV & other streaming services. The fully-equipped kitchen features an induction stove and plenty of amenities to cook meals for your party. The 8' farm table comfortably seats 8 people. The sunroom windows feature pull-down screens to enjoy the breeze and plenty of natural light. The downstairs master features a king bed, walk-in closet, and ensuite full bathroom. The front hallway has a half bath. Upstairs, enjoy another sitting area with another large TV (55"), bookshelf, playing cards, poker chips, and plenty of board games. If the couch doesn't provide enough space, feel free to grab our 4 colorful bean bags off the landing. Kids love these!! We provide an acoustic guitar, so don't worry about packing your own. For the 3 upstairs bedrooms: the first features a king bed, the second features 2 queen beds, and the third features a twin-over-full bunk bed. There's also a full bathroom. Outside, we have a Weber grill on the back patio and, again, seating for 8 on our patio set with the red umbrella. We also offer a "playroom" garage equipped with our third flat-screen TV, soundbar, ping pong table, darts board, cooler, and cornhole . In the front yard, enjoy our custom built fire pit with bench seating around our Yukon 27" Solo Stove. In the "attached" garage, we provide a folding table, folding chairs, camp chairs, and a portable cooler. And a short walk (6min) from our property, you'll access 40 acres of private eco-village trails that are PERFECT for a morning stroll or evening saunter!! Highlights include a hot tub, outdoor shower, 10-person outdoor dining table, outdoor living space, grill, fire pit, 12-person indoor dining table, heated floors, and a spectacular well-stocked kitchen. It is the perfect location for large groups (up to 11 people) wishing to explore the area, or to just relax in this beautiful home. The Treehouse is minutes away from popular wineries, breweries, distilleries, farms, hiking trails, and other attractions. It is 30 minutes from Charlottesville, and 15 minutes from Crozet and Waynesboro. The Treehouse was featured in the Fall 2023 C-Ville Abode Magazine (article titled "Hillside Haven") and is a 2025 Best of C-Ville Finalist. My name is Lauren Shifflett, and my husband and I manage our small farm here in Schuyler, Virginia. I have always dreamed of running my own homestead as I have always had a passion for animals and desire to be self sufficient.

Over the last year I have maintained my sourdough starters and baked a variety of different sourdough items that we love. Turns out, a lot of other people love them too so I completed my Food Handler's Certification and began a small in home bakery offering a multiple list of baked goods. After seeing the love for my baked goods, I wanted to continue to learn and do more with our farm.

Glass Hollow Studio and Gallery

Discover the art of glassmaking at Glass Hollow Studio and Gallery, nestled in the scenic Rockfish Valley. This unique destination offers visitors the opportunity to witness skilled artisans at work and explore beautiful handcrafted glass pieces in their gallery.

Location: 9080 Rockfish Valley Highway, Afton, VA
Hours: Thursday - Sunday, 11am - 5pm
Contact: (434) 270-6104 | glasshollow.com

Special Events

Join Glass Hollow for their popular Make Your Own Glass Pumpkin workshops, held every Saturday in September. These hands-on experiences allow visitors to create their own unique glass pumpkin keepsake under expert guidance. Advanced registration is required through their website.

Whether you're interested in watching the mesmerizing process of glassblowing or trying your hand at creating your own piece, Glass Hollow Studio and Gallery offers an unforgettable experience in the heart of Nelson County.
